contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #056: Termination of projective and Kähler fourfold minimal model programs.

Y is a normal irreducible compact complex analytic fourfold with ordinary terminal singularities. The fixed projective resolution g:Ytilde->Y has smooth source, is an isomorphism over Yreg, has a simple-normal-crossing exceptional divisor, and principalizes the singular ideal. T is an irreducible curve component of Sing(Y); T0 is its connected smooth open after finitely many punctures on which the stated cohomology sheaves are local systems.

definitions.a: ordinary LOG discrepancy, equal to one plus the relative canonical coefficient
definitions.global_place: prime divisor on a normal proper bimeromorphic model of the whole compact Y, up to common-model strict transform
definitions.N: number of prime components E of Exc(g) with g(E)=T and a(E;Y,0)=2

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 056 (Termination of projective and Kähler fourfold minimal model programs.; papers: Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds; Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds; Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary; Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds; Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
With Y additionally Kahler, b <= N. The right side counts distinct global prime divisorial places, not local branches.
Canonical restriction induces a monodromy-equivariant surjection q:W->V. On each stalk it is restriction from H^2(g^{-1}(t),Q), via neighborhoods, to H^2 of punctured regular neighborhoods.
W has finite monodromy. Consequently b is the invariant dimension of V and the canonical surjection q has b global flat sections of W whose images are fiberwise linearly independent.

There exist a loop-preserving curve domain B in T0, a small projective crepant terminal model ell over a Stein neighborhood of a full compact Kprime, and b line bundles N_i on that model whose regular-locus classes agree with one common positive multiple of b independent invariant punctured classes. Factoriality is used only over the full Kprime before restriction.

For the CP_COMPACT construction, the degree map Q^b->Q^s on the s irreducible surface families over B is injective. Thus s>=b; each fiber curve is accounted for, including normalization-cover sheets and nonreduced fibers.

After the finite puncturing making each global exceptional divisor a smooth connected-fiber family over a connected finite etale Stein-factor cover, every connected B in T0 surjecting on pi_1(T0) has the following property: restriction is a bijection from all global ordinary-log-discrepancy-two places centered at T to all local ordinary-log-discrepancy-two places centered at B in an ambient open with intersection T equal to B. All are represented on g.

The same bound b<=N and the CP_GLOBAL bijection hold without assuming that the compact complex fourfold Y is Kahler, provided the specified globally projective resolution and the other hypotheses in the context are retained.

Conditional on the separate topological estimate beta(Q)-sum c2(Q_j^nu)<=sum_{T subset Sing(Y) cap Q} b_T, CP_BOUND gives beta(Q)<=sum c2(Q_j^nu)+tau_Y(Q). Together with the stated local bracket and weight bounds of Section 07, this implies nonnegative junction difficulty; those separate bounds are not certified by this mission.

external_assumptions.statement: For analytic normal surface resolutions, exceptional intersection matrices are negative definite and exceptional smooth rational (-1)-curves contract to smooth points. With the local rationality and adjunction argument in report Appendix A, this implies terminal fourfolds are smooth in codimension two.
external_assumptions.source: Classical analytic surface theory (Grauert exceptional-curve criterion), used as a source-only assumption; original Grauert text was not retrieved. The staged October 6 canonical manuscript Lemma 2.3 and report Appendix A give the local reduction, without a termination theorem.

routes.retired_because: Counting local surfaces over a simply connected disc does not control distinct global divisors: removing the loop of a transitive two-sheet cover splits its one orbit into two. This rejects the shortcut only, not the geometric bound; an arbitrary permutation example is not a fourfold counterexample.

A surjection of local systems need not be surjective on invariant sections without finite monodromy or another justified exactness input: the unipotent two-dimensional quotient control has no invariant lift of its nonzero quotient class. CP_MONODROMY supplies the missing geometric proof.
